title: The ideal gas equation
text: For a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, pressure and volume are inversely related: if the pressure is doubled, the volume is halved. This is Boyle's law. At constant pressure, the volume of a fixed amount of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature, measured in kelvin; this is Charles's law. The two laws combine with Avogadro's principle into the ideal gas equation, PV = nRT, where n is the amount of gas in moles and R is the molar gas constant, 8.314 J mol^-1 K^-1. Standard temperature and pressure (STP) in this course means 273.15 K and 101.325 kPa. Under these conditions one mole of an ideal gas occupies about 22.4 L. Real gases depart from ideal behaviour at high pressure and low temperature, where molecular volume and intermolecular attraction can no longer be ignored.

title: Projectile motion
text: A projectile is any object that moves only under the influence of gravity after it is launched. In this course, air resistance is neglected and the acceleration due to gravity, g, is taken as 9.81 m s^-2, acting vertically downward. The horizontal component of velocity therefore stays constant throughout the flight, while the vertical component changes at the rate g. For a projectile launched from level ground with speed u at an angle theta above the horizontal, the time of flight is 2u sin(theta) / g and the horizontal range is u^2 sin(2 theta) / g. Because sin(2 theta) is largest when 2 theta is 90 degrees, the range on level ground is greatest at a launch angle of 45 degrees. At the highest point of the path the vertical velocity is zero, but the horizontal velocity is not.

title: Binary search
text: Binary search finds a target value in a list that is already sorted. It compares the target with the middle element. If they are equal, the search ends. If the target is smaller, the search continues in the left half; if it is larger, in the right half. Each comparison discards half of the remaining elements, so the worst-case number of comparisons grows with the logarithm of the list length: its time complexity is O(log n). A sorted list of 1,000 items needs at most 10 comparisons, because 2^10 = 1,024 is the first power of two greater than 1,000. Binary search does not work on an unsorted list; such a list must first be sorted or searched with linear search, which has time complexity O(n).

title: Cassava processing and cyanide
text: Cassava roots contain cyanogenic glucosides, mainly linamarin, which release hydrogen cyanide when the plant tissue is damaged. Processing reduces this hazard. To make garri, peeled roots are grated, packed into sacks and left to ferment for two to four days while water is pressed out; the mash is then sieved and roasted. Grating breaks the cells so that the enzyme linamarase can act on linamarin, and roasting drives off much of the remaining hydrogen cyanide. Sun-drying of thin chips also lowers cyanide content, but more slowly. For this course, a total cyanide content of 10 mg per kg in the finished flour is the reference safety limit. Poorly processed cassava has been linked to konzo, a paralytic disease, in communities that depend heavily on cassava during food shortages.

title: Gram staining
text: Gram staining sorts most bacteria into two groups by the structure of their cell walls. A heat-fixed smear is first flooded with crystal violet, the primary stain. Iodine is then added as a mordant, forming a crystal violet-iodine complex inside the cells. Next, the smear is washed briefly with alcohol or acetone, the decolouriser. Gram-positive cells, whose walls have a thick layer of peptidoglycan, keep the purple complex. Gram-negative cells, with a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane, lose it. Finally, safranin is applied as the counterstain, so gram-negative cells appear pink or red under the microscope while gram-positive cells stay purple. Decolourising for too long is the most common error: it can make gram-positive cells look gram-negative.

title: Concrete mix and curing
text: Concrete is a mixture of cement, fine aggregate (sand), coarse aggregate (gravel or crushed stone) and water. A nominal mix of 1:2:4 means one part cement, two parts sand and four parts coarse aggregate by volume. The water-cement ratio controls strength more than any other single factor: adding extra water makes concrete easier to place but weaker and more porous when it hardens. After placing, concrete must be cured, that is, kept moist and at a suitable temperature, so that the cement continues to hydrate. In this course the minimum curing period for ordinary Portland cement concrete is seven days. Design strength is specified as the compressive strength reached at 28 days, measured by crushing standard cubes in the laboratory.

title: Mean, median and mode
text: Measures of central tendency summarise a data set with a single typical value. The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. The median is the middle value when the data are arranged in order; with an even number of values it is the average of the two middle values. The mode is the value that occurs most often, and a data set may have more than one mode or none. For the quiz scores 4, 7, 7, 9 and 13, the sum is 40, so the mean is 8; the median is 7; and the mode is 7. The mean is sensitive to extreme values, so when a data set contains outliers the median often gives a better picture of a typical value.

title: Price elasticity of demand
text: Price elasticity of demand measures how strongly the quantity demanded responds to a change in price. It is calculated as the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. Because price and quantity demanded usually move in opposite directions, the coefficient is normally negative, and economists often compare its absolute value. Demand is elastic when the absolute value is greater than 1, inelastic when it is less than 1, and unit elastic when it equals 1. For example, if the price of a bag of rice rises by 10 percent and the quantity demanded falls by 25 percent, the elasticity is -2.5, so demand is elastic. When demand is elastic, a price increase lowers total revenue.

title: Spaced repetition
text: Spaced repetition is a study method in which material is reviewed at increasing intervals instead of being crammed in a single session. A student might review new lecture notes one day after the lecture, again three days later, then a week later and then a month later. Each review is most useful when it requires active recall, such as answering practice questions from memory, rather than simply rereading. The method works because memories that are retrieved after some forgetting has begun are strengthened more than memories retrieved immediately. Flashcards and past-question practice are common ways to apply it. Spacing does not reduce the total effort needed, but it makes the same effort last longer.

title: Database normalisation
text: Normalisation organises the tables of a relational database to reduce redundancy and update anomalies. A table is in first normal form (1NF) when every column holds atomic values and there are no repeating groups. It is in second normal form (2NF) when it is in 1NF and every non-key column depends on the whole primary key, not just part of a composite key. It is in third normal form (3NF) when it is in 2NF and no non-key column depends on another non-key column, a situation called a transitive dependency. For example, if a Students table stores both a department code and the department's name, the name depends on the code rather than on the student, so the table is not in 3NF; the department name should move to a separate Departments table.
